rules.subject: GENERAL DESCRIPTION
rules.text: Numeric. An arithmetic expression must be specified. The value of the arithmetic expression, including operational sign, is used in determining the value of the function.

rules.subject: GENERAL DESCRIPTION
rules.text: Alphabetic. An elementary data item of the class alphabetic or a nonnumeric literal containing only alphabetic characters must be specified. The size associated with the argument can be used in determining the value of the function.

rules.subject: GENERAL DESCRIPTION
rules.text: Alphanumeric. A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric or a nonnumeric literal must be specified. The size associated with the argument can be used in determining the value of the function.

rules.subject: GENERAL DESCRIPTION
rules.text:
Integer. An arithmetic expression which will always result in an integer value must be specified. The value of the arithmetic expression, including operational sign, is used in determining the value of the function.
The rules for a function may place constraints on the permissible values for arguments in order to permit meaningful determination of the function's value. If, at the time a function is referenced, the arguments specified for that reference do not have values within the permissible range, the returned value for the function is undefined.
When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times, a table may be referenced by specifying the data-name and any qualifiers that identify the table, followed immediately by subscripting where one or more of the subscripts is the word ALL.
When ALL is specified as a subscript, the effect is as if each table element associated with that subscript position were specified. The order of the implicit specification of each occurrence is from left to right, with the first (or leftmost) specification being the identifier with each subscript specified by the word ALL replaced by one, the next specification being the same identifier with the rightmost subscript specified by the word ALL incremented by one. This process continues with the rightmost ALL subscript being incremented by one for each implicit specification until the rightmost ALL subscript has been incremented through its range of values. If there are any additional ALL subscripts, the ALL subscript immediately to the left of the rightmost ALL subscript is incremented by one, the rightmost ALL subscript is reset to one and the process of varying the rightmost ALL subscript is repeated. The ALL subscript to the left of the rightmost ALL subscript is incremented by one through its range of values. For each additional ALL subscript, this process is repeated in turn until the leftmost ALL subscript has been incremented by one through its range of values. If
the ALL subscript is associated with an OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause, the range of values is determined by the object of the OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause. The evaluation of an ALL subscript must result in at least one argument, otherwise the returned value is undefined.

rules.subject: GENERAL DESCRIPTION
rules.text: Alphanumeric functions. These are of the class and category alphanumeric. The number of character positions in this data item is specified in the function definition. Alphanumeric functions have an implicit usage of DISPLAY.

rules.subject: GENERAL DESCRIPTION
rules.text:
Numeric functions. These are of the class and category numeric. A numeric function is always considered to have an operational sign. Those characteristics of the returned value not otherwise specified for a given function are defined by the implementor.
A numeric function may be used only in an arithmetic expression.
A numeric function may not be referenced where an integer operand is required, even though a particular reference may yield an integer value.

rules.subject: GENERAL DESCRIPTION
rules.text:
Integer functions. These are of the class and category numeric. An integer function is always considered to have an operational sign. Those characteristics of the returned value not otherwise specified for a given function are defined by the implementor.
An integer function may be used only in an arithmetic expression.
An integer function can be referenced where an integer operand is required and where a signed operand is allowed.

rules.subject: THE ACOS FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION ACOS ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE ACOS FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE ACOS FUNCTION
rules.text: The value of argument-1 must be greater than or equal to -1 and less than or equal to +1.

rules.subject: THE ACOS FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the approximation of the arccosine of argument-1 and is greater than or equal to zero and less than or equal to pi.

rules.subject: THE ANNUITY FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION ANNUITY ( argument-1 argument-2 )

rules.subject: THE ANNUITY FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE ANNUITY FUNCTION
rules.text: The value of argument-1 must be greater than or equal to zero.

rules.subject: THE ANNUITY FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-2 must be a positive integer.

rules.subject: THE ANNUITY FUNCTION
rules.text:
When the value of argument-1 is zero, the value of the function is the approximation of:
1 / argument-2

rules.subject: THE ANNUITY FUNCTION
rules.text:
When the value of argument-1 is not zero, the value of the function is the approximation of:
argument-1 / (1 - (1 + argument-1) \*\* (- argument-2))

rules.subject: THE ASIN FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION ASIN ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE ASIN FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE ASIN FUNCTION
rules.text: The value of argument-1 must be greater than or equal to -1 and less than or equal to +1.

rules.subject: THE ASIN FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the approximation of the arcsine of argument-1 and is greater than or equal to -pi/2 and less than or equal to +pi/2.

rules.subject: THE ATAN FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION ATAN ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE ATAN FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE ATAN FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the approximation of the arctangent of argument-1 and is greater than -pi/2 and less than +pi/2.

rules.subject: THE CHAR FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION CHAR ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE CHAR FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be an integer.

rules.subject: THE CHAR FUNCTION
rules.text: The value of argument-1 must be greater than zero and less than or equal to the number of positions in the collating sequence.

rules.subject: THE CHAR FUNCTION
rules.text: If more than one character has the same position in the program collating sequence, the character returned as the function value is that of the first literal specified for that character position in the ALPHABET clause.

rules.subject: THE CHAR FUNCTION
rules.text: If the current program collating sequence was not specified by an ALPHABET clause, the implementor determines the value.

rules.subject: THE COS FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION COS ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE COS FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE COS FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the approximation of the cosine of argument-1 and is greater than or equal to -1 and less than or equal to +1.

rules.subject: THE CURRENT-DATE FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE

rules.subject: THE CURRENT-DATE FUNCTION
rules.text:
The character positions returned, numbered from left to right, are:
| Character Positions | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1-4 | Four numeric digits of the year in the Gregorian calendar. |
| 5-6 | Two numeric digits of the month of the year, in the range 01 through 12. |
| 7-8 | Two numeric digits of the day of the month, in the range 01 through 31. |
| 9-10 | Two numeric digits of the hours past midnight, in the range 00 through 23. |
| 11-12 | Two numeric digits of the minutes past the hour, in the range 00 through 59. |
| 13-14 | Two numeric digits of the seconds past the minute, in the range 00 through 59. |
| 15-16 | Two numeric digits of the hundredths of a second past the second, in the range 00 through 99. The value 00 is returned if the system on which the function is evaluated does not have the facility to provide the fractional part of a second. |
| 17 | Either the character '-', the character '+', or the character '0'. The character '-' is returned if the local time indicated in the previous character positions is behind Greenwich Mean Time. The character '+' is returned if the local time indicated is the same as or ahead of Greenwich Mean Time. The character '0' is returned if the system on which this function is evaluated does not have the facility to provide the local time differential factor. |
| 18-19 | If character position 17 is '-', two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 12 indicating the number of hours that the reported time is behind Greenwich Mean Time. If character position 17 is '+', two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 13 indicating the number of hours that the reported time is ahead of Greenwich Mean Time. If character position 17 is '0', the value 00 is returned. |
| Character Positions | Contents |
|---|---|
| 20-21 | Two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 59 indicating the number of additional minutes that the reported time is ahead of or behind Greenwich Mean Time, depending on whether character position 17 is '+' or '-', respectively. If character position 17 is '0', the value 00 is returned. |

rules.subject: THE CURRENT-DATE FUNCTION
rules.text: If the system does not have the facility to provide fractional parts of a second, the value 00 is returned in character positions 15 and 16.

rules.subject: THE CURRENT-DATE FUNCTION
rules.text: If the system does not have the facility to provide the local time differential factor, the value 00000 is returned in character positions 17 through 21.

rules.subject: THE DATE-OF-INTEGER FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE DATE-OF-INTEGER FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 is a positive integer that represents a number of days succeeding December 31, 1600, in the Gregorian calendar.

rules.subject: THE DATE-OF-INTEGER FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value represents the ISO Standard date equivalent of the integer specified in argument-1.

rules.subject: THE DATE-OF-INTEGER FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is in the form (YYYYMMDD) where YYYY represents a year in the Gregorian calendar; MM represents the month of that year; and DD represents the day of that month.

rules.subject: THE DAY-OF-INTEGER FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION DAY-OF-INTEGER ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE DAY-OF-INTEGER FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 is a positive integer that represents a number of days succeeding December 31, 1600, in the Gregorian calendar.

rules.subject: THE DAY-OF-INTEGER FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value represents the Julian equivalent of the integer specified in argument-1.

rules.subject: THE DAY-OF-INTEGER FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is an integer of the form (YYYYDDD) where YYYY represents a year in the Gregorian calendar and DDD represents the day of that year.

rules.subject: THE FACTORIAL FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION FACTORIAL ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE FACTORIAL FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be an integer greater than or equal to zero.

rules.subject: THE FACTORIAL FUNCTION
rules.text: If the value of argument-1 is zero, the value 1 is returned.

rules.subject: THE FACTORIAL FUNCTION
rules.text: If the value of argument-1 is positive, its factorial is returned.

rules.subject: THE INTEGER FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION INTEGER ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE INTEGER FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE INTEGER FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the greatest integer less than or equal to the value of argument-1. For example, if the value of argument-1 is -1.5, -2 is returned. If the value of argument-1 is +1.5, +1 is returned.

rules.subject: THE INTEGER-OF-DATE FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE INTEGER-OF-DATE FUNCTION
rules.text:
Argument-1 must be an integer of the form YYYYMMDD, whose value is obtained from the calculation (YYYY * 10,000) + (MM * 100) + DD.
a. YYYY represents the year in the Gregorian calendar. It must be an integer greater than 1600.
b. MM represents a month and must be a positive integer less than 13.
c. DD represents a day and must be a positive integer less than 32 provided that it is valid for the specified month and year combination.

rules.subject: THE INTEGER-OF-DATE FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is an integer that is the number of days the date represented by argument-1 succeeds December 31, 1600, in the Gregorian calendar.

rules.subject: THE INTEGER-OF-DAY FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DAY ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE INTEGER-OF-DAY FUNCTION
rules.text:
Argument-1 must be an integer of the form YYYYDDD, whose value is obtained from the calculation (YYYY \* 1000) + DDD.
a. YYYY represents the year in the Gregorian calendar. It must be an integer greater than 1600.
b. DDD represents the day of the year. It must be a positive integer less than 367 provided that it is valid for the year specified.

rules.subject: THE INTEGER-OF-DAY FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is an integer that is the number of days the date represented by argument-1 succeeds December 31, 1600, in the Gregorian calendar.

rules.subject: THE INTEGER-PART FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION INTEGER-PART ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE INTEGER-PART FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE INTEGER-PART FUNCTION
rules.text: If the value of argument-1 is zero, the returned value is zero.

rules.subject: THE INTEGER-PART FUNCTION
rules.text: If the value of argument-1 is positive, the returned value is the greatest integer less than or equal to the value of argument-1. For example, if the value of argument-1 is +1.5, +1 is returned.

rules.subject: THE INTEGER-PART FUNCTION
rules.text: If the value of argument-1 is negative, the returned value is the least integer greater than or equal to the value of argument-1. For example, if the value of argument-1 is -1.5, -1 is returned.

rules.subject: THE LENGTH FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION LENGTH ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE LENGTH FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 may be a nonnumeric literal or a data item of any class or category.

rules.subject: THE LENGTH FUNCTION
rules.text: If argument-1 or any data item subordinate to argument-1 is described with the DEPENDING phrase of the OCCURS clause, the contents of the data item referenced by the data-name specified in the DEPENDING phrase are used at the time the LENGTH function is evaluated.

rules.subject: THE LENGTH FUNCTION
rules.text: If argument-1 is a nonnumeric literal or an elementary data item or argument-1 is a group data item that does not contain a variable occurrence data item, the value returned is an integer equal to the length of argument-1 in character positions.

rules.subject: THE LENGTH FUNCTION
rules.text: If argument-1 is a group data item containing a variable occurrence data item, the returned value is an integer determined by evaluation of the data item specified in the DEPENDING phrase of the OCCURS clause for that variable occurrence data item. This evaluation is accomplished according to the rules in the OCCURS clause dealing with the data item as a sending data item. (See page VI-26, The OCCURS Clause; and page VI-46, The USAGE Clause.)

rules.subject: THE LENGTH FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value includes implicit FILLER characters, if any.

rules.subject: THE LOG FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION LOG ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE LOG FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE LOG FUNCTION
rules.text: The value of argument-1 must be greater than zero.

rules.subject: THE LOG FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the approximation of the logarithm to the base e of argument-1.

rules.subject: THE LOG10 FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION LOG10 ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE LOG10 FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE LOG10 FUNCTION
rules.text: The value of argument-1 must be greater than zero.

rules.subject: THE LOG10 FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the approximation of the logarithm to the base 10 of argument-1.

rules.subject: THE LOWER-CASE FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION LOWER-CASE ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE LOWER-CASE FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class alphabetic or alphanumeric and must be at least one character in length.

rules.subject: THE LOWER-CASE FUNCTION
rules.text: The same character string as argument-1 is returned, except that each uppercase letter replaced by the corresponding lowercase letter.

rules.subject: THE LOWER-CASE FUNCTION
rules.text: The character string returned has the same length as argument-1.

rules.subject: THE LOWER-CASE FUNCTION
rules.text: If the computer character set does not include lowercase letters, no changes take place in the character string.

rules.subject: THE MAX FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION MAX ( { argument-1 } … )

rules.subject: THE MAX FUNCTION
rules.text: If more than one argument-1 is specified, all arguments must be of the same class.

rules.subject: THE MAX FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the content of the argument-1 having the greatest value. The comparisons used to determine the greatest value are made according to the rules for simple conditions. (See page VI-54, Simple Conditions.)

rules.subject: THE MAX FUNCTION
rules.text: If more than one argument-1 has the same greatest value, the content of the argument-1 returned is the leftmost argument-1 having that value.

rules.subject: THE MAX FUNCTION
rules.text: If the type of the function is alphanumeric, the size of the returned value is the same as the size of the selected argument-1.

rules.subject: THE MEAN FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION MEAN ( { argument-1 } … )

rules.subject: THE MEAN FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE MEAN FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the arithmetic mean of the argument-1 series.

rules.subject: THE MEAN FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is defined as the sum of the argument-1 series divided by the number of occurrences referenced by argument-1.

rules.subject: THE MEDIAN FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION MEDIAN ( { argument-1 } … )

rules.subject: THE MEDIAN FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE MEDIAN FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the content of the argument-1 having the middle value in the list formed by arranging all the argument-1 values in sorted order.

rules.subject: THE MEDIAN FUNCTION
rules.text: If the number of occurrences referenced by argument-1 is odd, the returned value is such that at least half of the occurrences referenced by argument-1 are greater than or equal to the returned value and at least half are less than or equal. If the number of occurrences referenced by argument-1 is even, the returned value is the arithmetic mean of the values referenced by the two middle occurrences.

rules.subject: THE MEDIAN FUNCTION
rules.text: The comparisons used to arrange the argument-1 values in sorted order are made according to the rules for simple conditions. (See page VI-54, Simple Conditions.)

rules.subject: THE MIDRANGE FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION MIDRANGE ( { argument-1 } … )

rules.subject: THE MIDRANGE FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE MIDRANGE FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the arithmetic mean of the greatest argument-1 value and the least argument-1 value. The comparisons used to determine the greatest and least values are made according to the rules for simple conditions. (See page VI-54, Simple Conditions.)

rules.subject: THE MIN FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION MIN ( { argument-1 } … )

rules.subject: THE MIN FUNCTION
rules.text: If more than one argument-1 is specified, all arguments must be of the same class.

rules.subject: THE MIN FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the content of the argument-1 having the least value. The comparisons used to determine the least value are made according to the rules for simple conditions. (See page VI-54, Simple Conditions.)

rules.subject: THE MIN FUNCTION
rules.text: If more than one argument-1 has the same least value, the content of the argument-1 returned is the leftmost argument-1 having that value.

rules.subject: THE MIN FUNCTION
rules.text: If the type of the function is alphanumeric, the size of the returned value is the same as the size of the selected argument-1.

rules.subject: THE MOD FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION MOD ( argument-1 argument-2 )

rules.subject: THE MOD FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 and argument-2 must be integers.

rules.subject: THE MOD FUNCTION
rules.text: The value of argument-2 must not be zero.

rules.subject: THE MOD FUNCTION
rules.text:
The returned value is argument-1 modulo argument-2. The returned value is defined as:
argument-1 - (argument-2 \* FUNCTION INTEGER (argument-1 / argument-2))

rules.subject: THE MOD FUNCTION
rules.text:
The following illustrates the expected results for some values of argument-1 and argument-2.
| <u>Argument-1</u> | <u>Argument-2</u> | <u>Return</u> |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | 5 | 1 |
| -11 | 5 | 4 |
| 11 | -5 | -4 |
| -11 | -5 | -1 |

rules.subject: THE NUMVAL FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION NUMVAL ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE NUMVAL FUNCTION
rules.text:
Argument-1 must be a nonnumeric literal or alphanumeric data item whose content has one of the following two formats: 
┌ + ┐ ╭ digit [ . [digit]] ╮
[space] │ │ [space] ┤ ├ [space]
└ - ┘ ╰ . digit ╯
or 
┌ + ┐
│ │
╭ digit [ . [digit]] ╮ │ - │
[space] ┤ ├ [space] │ │ [space]
╰ . digit ╯ │ CR │
│ │
└ DB ┘
where space is a string of zero or more spaces and digit is a string of one to 18 digits.

rules.subject: THE NUMVAL FUNCTION
rules.text: The total number of digits in argument-1 must not exceed 18.

rules.subject: THE NUMVAL FUNCTION
rules.text: If the DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA clause is specified in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, a comma must be used in argument-1 rather than a decimal point.

rules.subject: THE NUMVAL FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the numeric value represented by argument-1.

rules.subject: THE NUMVAL FUNCTION
rules.text: The number of digits returned is 18.

rules.subject: THE NUMVAL-C FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION NUMVAL-C ( argument-1 [ argument-2 ] )

rules.subject: THE NUMVAL-C FUNCTION
rules.text:
Argument-1 must be a nonnumeric literal or alphanumeric data item whose content has one of the following two formats: 
┌ + ┐ ╭ digit [, digit] … [. [digit]] ╮
[space] │ │ [space] [cs] [space] ┤ ├ [space]
└ - ┘ ╰ . digit ╯
or 
┌ + ┐
╭ digit [, digit] … [. [digit]] ╮ │ - │
[space] [cs] [space] ┤ ├ [space] │ │ [space]
╰ . digit ╯ │ CR │
└ DB ┘
where space is a string of zero or more spaces, cs is the string of one or more characters specified by argument-2 and digit is a string of one or more digits.

rules.subject: THE NUMVAL-C FUNCTION
rules.text: If the DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA clause is specified in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, the functions of the comma and decimal point in argument-1 are reversed.

rules.subject: THE NUMVAL-C FUNCTION
rules.text: The total number of digits in argument-1 must not exceed 18.

rules.subject: THE NUMVAL-C FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-2, if specified, must be a nonnumeric literal or alphanumeric data item.

rules.subject: THE NUMVAL-C FUNCTION
rules.text: If argument-2 is not specified, the character used for cs is the currency symbol specified for the program.

rules.subject: THE NUMVAL-C FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the numeric value represented by argument-1.

rules.subject: THE NUMVAL-C FUNCTION
rules.text: The number of digits returned is 18.

rules.subject: THE ORD FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION ORD ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE ORD FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be one character in length and must be class alphabetic or alphanumeric.

rules.subject: THE ORD FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the ordinal position of argument-1 in the collating sequence for the program.

rules.subject: THE ORD-MAX FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION ORD-MAX ( { argument-1 } … )

rules.subject: THE ORD-MAX FUNCTION
rules.text: If more than one argument-1 is specified, all arguments must be of the same class.

rules.subject: THE ORD-MAX FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the ordinal number that corresponds to the position of the argument-1 having the greatest value in the argument-1 series.

rules.subject: THE ORD-MAX FUNCTION
rules.text: The comparisons used to determine the greatest valued argument are made according to the rules for simple conditions. (See page VI-54, Simple Conditions.)

rules.subject: THE ORD-MAX FUNCTION
rules.text: If more than one argument-1 has the same greatest value, the number returned corresponds to the position of the leftmost argument-1 having that value.

rules.subject: THE ORD-MIN FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION ORD-MIN ( { argument-1 } … )

rules.subject: THE ORD-MIN FUNCTION
rules.text: If more than one argument-1 is specified, all arguments must be of the same class.

rules.subject: THE ORD-MIN FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the ordinal number that corresponds to the position of the argument-1 having the least value in the argument-1 series.

rules.subject: THE ORD-MIN FUNCTION
rules.text: The comparisons used to determine the least valued argument-1 are made according to the rules for simple conditions. (See page VI-54, Simple Conditions.)

rules.subject: THE ORD-MIN FUNCTION
rules.text: If more than one argument-1 has the same least value, the number returned corresponds to the position of the leftmost argument-1 having that value.

rules.subject: THE PRESENT-VALUE FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE ( argument-1 { argument-2 } … )

rules.subject: THE PRESENT-VALUE FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 and argument-2 must be of the class numeric.

rules.subject: THE PRESENT-VALUE FUNCTION
rules.text: The value of argument-1 must be greater than -1.

rules.subject: THE PRESENT-VALUE FUNCTION
rules.text:
The returned value is an approximation of the summation of a series of calculations with each term in the following form:
argument-2 / (1 + argument-1) ** n
There is one term for each occurrence of argument-2. The exponent, n, is incremented from one by one for each term in the series.
<invoking-skill>Intrinsic Function - RANDOM

rules.subject: THE RANDOM FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION RANDOM [ ( argument-1 ) ]

rules.subject: THE RANDOM FUNCTION
rules.text: If argument-1 is specified, it must be zero or a positive integer. It is used as the seed value to generate a sequence of pseudo-random numbers.

rules.subject: THE RANDOM FUNCTION
rules.text: If a subsequent reference specifies argument-1, a new sequence of pseudo-random numbers is started.

rules.subject: THE RANDOM FUNCTION
rules.text: If the first reference to this function in the run unit does not specify argument-1, the seed value is defined by the implementor.

rules.subject: THE RANDOM FUNCTION
rules.text: In each case, subsequent references without specifying argument-1 return the next number in the current sequence.

rules.subject: THE RANDOM FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is greater than or equal to zero and less than one.

rules.subject: THE RANDOM FUNCTION
rules.text: For a given seed value on a given implementation, the sequence of pseudo-random numbers will always be the same.

rules.subject: THE RANDOM FUNCTION
rules.text:
The implementor will specify the subset of the domain of argument-1 values that will yield distinct sequences of pseudo-random numbers. This subset must include the values from 0 through at least 32767.
A-64</invoking-skill>

rules.subject: THE RANGE FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION RANGE ( { argument-1 } … )

rules.subject: THE RANGE FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE RANGE FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is equal to the greatest value of argument-1 minus the least value of argument-1. The comparisons used to determine the greatest and least values are made according to the rules for simple conditions. (See page VI-54, Simple Conditions.)

rules.subject: THE REM FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION REM ( argument-1 argument-2 )

rules.subject: THE REM FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 and argument-2 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE REM FUNCTION
rules.text: The value of argument-2 must not be zero.

rules.subject: THE REM FUNCTION
rules.text:
The returned value is the remainder of argument-1 / argument-2. It is defined as the expression: 
argument-1 - (argument-2 * FUNCTION INTEGER-PART (argument-1 / argument-2))

rules.subject: THE REVERSE FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION REVERSE ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE REVERSE FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class alphabetic or alphanumeric and must be at least one character in length.

rules.subject: THE REVERSE FUNCTION
rules.text: If argument-1 is a character string of length n, the returned value is a character string of length n such that for 1 ≤ j ≤ n, the character in position j of the returned value is the character from position n-j+1 of argument-1.

rules.subject: THE SIN FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION SIN ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE SIN FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE SIN FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the approximation of the sine of argument-1 and is greater than or equal to -1 and less than or equal to +1.

rules.subject: THE SQRT FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION SQRT ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE SQRT FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE SQRT FUNCTION
rules.text: The value of argument-1 must be zero or positive.

rules.subject: THE SQRT FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the absolute value of the approximation of the square root of argument-1.

rules.subject: THE STANDARD-DEVIATION FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION ( { argument-1 } … )

rules.subject: THE STANDARD-DEVIATION FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE STANDARD-DEVIATION FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the approximation of the standard deviation of the argument-1 series.

rules.subject: THE STANDARD-DEVIATION FUNCTION
rules.text:
The returned value is calculated as follows:
a. The difference between each argument-1 value and the arithmetic mean of the argument-1 series is calculated and squared.
b. The values obtained are then added together. This quantity is divided by the number of values in the argument-1 series.
c. The square root of the quotient obtained is then calculated. The returned value is the absolute value of this square root.

rules.subject: THE STANDARD-DEVIATION FUNCTION
rules.text: If the argument-1 series consists of only one value, or if the argument-1 series consists of all variable occurrence data items and the total number of occurrences for all of them is one, the returned value is zero.

rules.subject: THE SUM FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION SUM ( { argument-1 } … )

rules.subject: THE SUM FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE SUM FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the sum of the arguments.

rules.subject: THE SUM FUNCTION
rules.text: If the argument-1 series are all integers, the value returned is an integer.

rules.subject: THE SUM FUNCTION
rules.text: If the argument-1 series are not all integers, a numeric value is returned.

rules.subject: THE TAN FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION TAN ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE TAN FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE TAN FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the approximation of the tangent of argument-1.

rules.subject: THE UPPER-CASE FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION UPPER-CASE ( argument-1 )

rules.subject: THE UPPER-CASE FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class alphabetic or alphanumeric and must be at least one character in length.

rules.subject: THE UPPER-CASE FUNCTION
rules.text: The same character string as argument-1 is returned, except that each lowercase letter is replaced by the corresponding uppercase letter.

rules.subject: THE UPPER-CASE FUNCTION
rules.text: The character string returned has the same length as argument-1.

rules.subject: THE VARIANCE FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION VARIANCE ( { argument-1 } … )

rules.subject: THE VARIANCE FUNCTION
rules.text: Argument-1 must be class numeric.

rules.subject: THE VARIANCE FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the approximation of the variance of the argument-1 series.

rules.subject: THE VARIANCE FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is defined as the square of the standard deviation of the argument-1 series. (See page A-70, STANDARD-DEVIATION Returned Values, rule 2.)

rules.subject: THE VARIANCE FUNCTION
rules.text: If the argument-1 series consists of only one value, or if the argument-1 series consists of all variable occurrence data items and the total number of occurrences for all of them is one, the returned value is zero.

rules.subject: THE WHEN-COMPILED FUNCTION
rules.text: FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED

rules.subject: THE WHEN-COMPILED FUNCTION
rules.text:
The character positions returned, numbered from left to right, are:
| Positions | Contents |
|---|---|
| 1-4 | Four numeric digits of the year in the Gregorian calendar. |
| 5-6 | Two numeric digits of the month of the year, in the range 01 through 12. |
| 7-8 | Two numeric digits of the day of the month, in the range 01 through 31. |
| 9-10 | Two numeric digits of the hours past midnight, in the range 00 through 23. |
| 11-12 | Two numeric digits of the minutes past the hour, in the range 00 through 59. |
| 13-14 | Two numeric digits of the seconds past the minute, in the range 00 through 59. |
| 15-16 | Two numeric digits of the hundredths of a second past the second, in the range 00 through 99. The value 00 is returned if the system on which the program was compiled did not have the facility to provide the fractional part of a second. |
| 17 | Either the character '-', the character '+', or the character '0'. The character '-' is returned if the local time of compilation, reported in the previous character positions, is behind Greenwich Mean Time. The character '+' is returned if the reported time is the same as or ahead of Greenwich Mean Time. The character '0' is returned if the system on which the program was compiled did not have the facility to provide the local time differential factor. |
| 18-19 | If character position 17 is '-', two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 12 indicating the number of hours that the reported time is behind Greenwich Mean Time. If character position 17 is '+', two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 13 indicating the number of hours that the reported time is ahead of Greenwich Mean Time. If character position 17 is '0', the value 00 is returned. |
| Character Positions | Contents |
|---|---|
| 20-21 | Two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 59 indicating the number of additional minutes that the reported time is ahead of or behind Greenwich Mean Time, depending on whether character position 17 is '+' or '-', respectively. If character position 17 is '0', the value 00 is returned. |

rules.subject: THE WHEN-COMPILED FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value is the date and time of compilation of the source program that contains this function. If the program is a contained program, the returned value is the compilation date and time associated with the separately compiled program in which it is contained.

rules.subject: THE WHEN-COMPILED FUNCTION
rules.text: The returned value must denote the same time as the compilation date and time if provided in the listing of the source program and in the generated object code for the source program, although their representations and precisions may differ.

rules.subject: THE INSPECT STATEMENT
rules.text: For the purpose of determining its length, identifier-1 is treated as if it were a sending data item. (See page VI-26, The OCCURS Clause).

rules.subject: THE INSPECT STATEMENT
rules.text: Identifier-1 is a sending data item.

rules.subject: THE RECORD CLAUSE
rules.text: It is implementor defined whether format 3 of the RECORD clause produces fixed length records or variable length records.

rules.subject: THE OPEN STATEMENT
rules.text: If the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, the physical file is not affected and the following actions take place in the following order: a. A value is placed in the I-O status associated with file-name to indicate the condition that caused the OPEN statement to be unsuccessful. b. Any applicable USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure is executed. (See page VII-50, The USE Statement.)

rules.subject: THE WRITE STATEMENT
rules.text: If the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful, the I-O status of the file-name associated with record-name-1 is updated and control is transferred according to the rules of the USE statement following the execution of any USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure applicable to the file-name associated with record-name-1. (See page VII-50, The USE Statement).

A value is placed in the I-O status associated with file-name to indicate the condition that caused the OPEN statement to be unsuccessful. b. Any applicable USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure is executed. (See page VIII-35, The USE Statement.)

(See page IX-39, The USE Statement.) IX-30 — Paragraph 4.5.4 of the READ statement in the Indexed I-O module, general rule 10b, change to read: b. If the AT END phrase is specified in the statement causing the condition, control is transferred to the AT END imperative-statement-1. Any USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1 is not executed. Execution then continues according to the rules for each statement specified in imperative-statement-1. If a procedure branching or conditional statement that causes explicit transfer of control is executed, control is transferred in accordance with the rules of that statement; otherwise, upon completion of the execution of imperative-statement-1 control is transferred to the end of the READ statement and the NOT AT END phrase, if specified, is ignored. IX-30 — Paragraph 4.5.4 of the READ statement in the Indexed I-O module, general rule 10c, replace the first sentence with the following: "If the AT END phrase is not specified, a USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure must be associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1, and that procedure is executed." IX-31 — Paragraph 4.5.4 of the READ statement in the Indexed I-O module, replace general rule 11b with the following: b. If an exception condition that is not an at end or an invalid key condition exists, control is transferred according to rules of the USE statement following the execution of any USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1. (See page IX-39, The USE Statement.)

rules.subject: THE EXIT PROGRAM STATEMENT
rules.text: ║(4) An EXIT PROGRAM statement must not be executed while executing within the range of a declarative procedure in which the GLOBAL phrase is specified, except within a program called while executing within the range of that declarative procedure.║

rules.subject: THE COPY STATEMENT
rules.text: The text produced as a result of the complete processing of a COPY statement must not contain a COPY statement.
